Configure the actor's extents to ten and eighteen and both fields at $E9F0 and $EA80 to three. Set the direct-shape flag at $EB10 and fall through to the shared colour and flag setup at $C34E.
Supply colour five. The common tail at $C350 stores A as the sprite colour, sets bit $04 in the actor flags and puts $0F in $E870.
End with extent values ten and eighteen, $E9F0 and $EA80 both three, sprite colour eight, actor flag bit $04 set and $E870 set to $0F.
Store sprite colour fourteen for the current actor slot in X.
Set both extent fields to three, $EA50 to $FF and the fields at $E9F0 and $EA80 to zero.

Set extent fields to nine and sixteen and fields at $E9F0 and $EA80 to three and five. Apply the shared setup at $C34E, then set horizontal movement to $10, $E840 to $14 and vertical movement to zero.
Clear the actor's visible flag $40 at $E810. The sprite pass at $2F62 requires that flag to gather the actor.
Set $EA50 to $FF, the fields at $E9F0 and $EA80 to four and six, and extents to eight and eleven. Continue into the visibility clear at $C3DF.
Set $EA50 to $FF and both extents to three. When the low three bits of $E810 are nonzero, copy them to $E840 and clear them from the flags.

Use the random value from $1A57 to choose whether to call $2927. Initialize extents to ten and eighteen and $E870 to four plus a two-bit random value. Set colour five, direct shape $95 and actor flag $04. Clear the horizontal and vertical movement fields and the counters at $E840, $E9C0 and $E750.
Set extents to fourteen and eighteen and both fields at $E9F0 and $EA80 to two, then enter the colour setup at $C350 with A set to fourteen.
The initializer for types $25, $33 and $36 immediately returns, preserving the defaults supplied by the engine.

Keep X at $CB46 and reset the shared bytes at $1D, $1F and $CB45. Initialize the actor and apply the flag and colour setup at $C4E9. Allocate children of types $27, $28 and $29 at its coordinates. Write their parent slot to $E900 and save the child slots at $CB47, $CB48 and $CB49.
Set sprite colour nine, set $EA50 to $FF and set actor flag bit $10. This is also used by the parent initializer at $C48B.
Set both extents to one. Set bits $34 in $E810 and bit $01 in $EB10. Set $EA50 to $FF and $E870 to $0F.
Set both movement fields to ten, set sprite colour one and return.
Set both actor extents to three and continue at $C404 to transfer the low flag bits into $E840.
A standalone RTS between the initializer and the next update entry.

When $1D is nonzero, save its low seven bits in $70 and set $1E to three. Allocate type $2A and copy the parent's coordinates, mark the source actor for removal, then pass the new slot to $3854 and set $4F to $FF.

Set horizontal movement to $10. If the resident check at $275A returns carry clear, $E840 is zero and the test at $2760 succeeds with A equal to ten, take the random branch whose low seven bits must be zero to spawn type $2E. Then pass four in $08 to the turn routine.

Take frame zero or two from the direction bit and pass it to $2742. Return if the resident test at $275A sets carry. Otherwise count down $E840, calling $2838 when it equals $E870. At zero call the turn logic with four in $08 and set horizontal movement to $15.
Call $279E with two. When it returns carry set, pass five to $2760 and return that check's carry to the caller.
On a successful proximity check, spawn three type $38 actors from the offsets starting at $C66D and flag the parent for removal.
On a successful proximity check, spawn four type $38 actors from the offsets starting at $C67C and flag the parent for removal.
On a successful proximity check, spawn four type $38 actors from the offsets starting at $C690 and flag the parent for removal.

Take the child type from A and the record count from Y. For each five-byte record at $3E/$3F, allocate a child, add the first two bytes to the parent's coarse X and Y, copy byte two into $E840 and $E870, and store the last two bytes as movement. Advance the record pointer by five and restore the parent slot in X.
The spawn loop at $C612 saves the requested child type here and reloads it for each allocation.

Twelve five-byte offset records. The three spawn entries read successive batches of three, four and four, leaving an additional record at $C6A4. The fields supply coarse offsets, two timers from one byte, and horizontal and vertical movement.
Decrement the timer at $E870, remove the actor on a negative result and otherwise call the resident check at $287A.
When $1F is set, increment the colour byte and make the actor visible. Test each active player with $23D6 unless $1D is negative. A successful test calls $216F and flags this actor for removal.

Clear horizontal movement and run the check at $275A. Animate using $C857 with a reset phase of three. Once the frame index reaches zero, count $E840 down. On underflow set movement to $20, reload the timer to two and update actor flag $04 and the $E870 cooldown.
Call $2927 and re-enter the initialization tail at $C42E.
Reset $E750 to three on underflow and toggle the low shape bit, using the actor direction to choose its two-shape pair. Continue at $C560.

When $E750 reaches zero, reload it to two and advance the four-state phase. Choose the group offset from the sign of vertical movement, or from the direction of nonzero horizontal movement when vertical movement is zero. Index $C791 with that offset ORed with the phase and pass control to $C560.
Four groups of four sprite pointers selected by $C748 for negative vertical, positive vertical, horizontal with flag $08 clear and horizontal with flag $08 set.
Call the resident check at $287A when the tile animation phase is four.

On carry from $22E5 increment coarse Y and call $381A. A zero $E840 removes the actor. Otherwise add $1A to the timer for the new type, remapping $20 to $25 and subtracting nine coarse rows in that case. Call $3854 and clear the removal flag. Test player proximity and, if both checks pass, stop horizontal motion with the parameter chosen by relative X.
Require a successful proximity check at $C5C5 to run the patrol update at $C560.
Move through $22E5 and call $2757 with four. Decrement $E840. At zero reload it with $14 and toggle direction flag $08.

Decrement the update timer at $C964. On underflow, reload ten and decrement the phase at $C965, wrapping from zero to four. Copy 72 bytes forward from the phase's source offset into $7960–$79A7, replacing glyphs $2C–$34.
The update entry for types $25 and $33 immediately returns to the actor loop.

Decrement $E750 and return while it is nonnegative. On underflow reload it with five, then decrement the shape index at $E9C0. Replace a negative index with the incoming A. Use the actor direction bit $08 to select $C884 or $C888 and store the resulting shape pointer at $E7E0.
Four sprite pointers indexed by the animation counter when actor flag $08 is set.
Four sprite pointers for the opposite direction, indexed by the same animation counter when flag $08 is clear.
Source for phases zero and four. The 72 bytes replace playfield glyphs $2C–$34 in order.
Source for phases one and three. Nine consecutive eight-byte bitmaps replace glyphs $2C–$34.
Source for phase two, the middle of the five-phase sequence. Nine eight-byte glyphs are copied from here.
The updater decrements this byte on each call. Underflow triggers a copy and reloads $0A.
A five-state index decremented before lookup and reset to four on underflow.
The phase offsets are $00, $48, $90, $48 and $00, measured from the first 72-byte frame at $C88C.

Run the resident checks at $287A and $38BD. When $390C is zero, use the carry from $23B7 to choose colour nine or one. If $275A returns carry, set $390C to $14, restore type $26 and clear visibility before calling $38BD. Otherwise call $2742 with four while $CB45 is clear, call the movement update at $C9BD and toggle direction each time $E9C0 underflows.

While $E840 is nonnegative, clear direct-shape mode if $CB45 is zero. Otherwise use direct shape $91 and check the return path if vertical movement is $14. On timer underflow select direct shape $91, reload $E840 to $1E and set $CB45. Change zero vertical movement to $EB and change $EB to $14.

At coarse row $0D clear direct-shape mode and vertical movement. Reload $E840 from the random value masked by $7F and ORed with $1C. Decrement $CB45 and clear the shape bytes for the five slot indices read from $CB46 through $CB4A.

Follow the parent at $E900 with a coarse X offset of three. Copy the other three coordinate bytes as they stand. Select direct shape $92 when $CB45 is set, or clear direct-shape mode and call $2742 with A set to four when it is zero.

Copy the parent's two X bytes and follow it with a Y offset of $0280 in the two-byte representation. Select direct shape $93 when $CB45 is set. Otherwise clear direct-shape mode and call $2742 with four.

Follow the parent with three added to coarse X and $0280 added to the two-byte Y coordinate. Use direct shape $94 when $CB45 is set. Otherwise clear direct-shape mode and call $2742 with four. Continue into the common child update.
Call the resident check at $287A and copy the parent's sprite colour. Mark the child for removal if $390C is set, the parent is no longer type $26, or its flags are zero or have bit zero set.
A jump to the return at $CB44 immediately after the shared child update's unconditional removal jump.
The parent sets this phase on movement timer expiry and decrements it on reaching coarse row $0D. Each child's update reads it to choose between its normal shape and a fixed direct shape.
The type $26 initializer writes its own slot here. The later routine at $CA3E reloads this slot.
Slot returned by the allocator for the parent's type $27 child.
Slot returned by the allocator for the parent's type $28 child.
Slot returned by the allocator for the parent's type $29 child.

Compare player zero's coarse coordinates to bounds derived from constants $CC and $27. Select an even relative-position index and read the corresponding pair from $CC07, storing it in scratch. Store its odd successor in the actor's $E870 field. The separate reset loop at $CA3E also uses this entry's opcode $AD as a fifth slot number.
Eight byte pairs selected by the relative-position branches at $CB4A. The routine copies the selected pair to zero-page scratch and to $CC21 and $CC22.
Values read at the odd indices selected by $CB4A. The lookup result goes to $09.
This byte receives the second byte in the chosen offset pair during the routine at $CB4A.
This byte receives the first byte in the chosen offset pair during the routine at $CB4A.
Compared against the adjacent offset byte loaded by the compare at $CBEE. The result controls whether the value table at $CC17 supplies the output.

Final two zero bytes of LEVELB's expanded image, emitted in the last repeat run before the $CC2D end pointer. The adjacent compare uses $CC2A and the indexed loads in $CB4A use positions derived from an even index no greater than fourteen and its successor.
